description: A decision conflicts with a recorded locked rule; another answers an open question; a number belongs to a lower layer of another system.
prompt: Use the design-capture skill. The docs are in this folder (start at README.md). My decisions from tonight: (1) You can pick arrows back up after a fight, from the ground and from corpses, so ammo is less punishing. (2) Arrows break against heavy armour. (3) For stamina, a full bow draw should cost 12 stamina per second, I'm pretty sure about that number. Record what you can.

assertions.desc: Quotes the conflicting rule ARC-R2 verbatim with its ID.
assertions.pattern: ARC-R2[\s\S]{0,300}Every arrow fired is consumed on impact|Every arrow fired is consumed on impact[\s\S]{0,300}ARC-R2

assertions.desc: Names the date the conflicting rule was decided (2026-10-02).
The reply says the new statement reverses a past ruling and asks which holds: new supersedes, old stays, or both stay tagged conflicting with an open question.
The archery spec records nothing about picking arrows up again (and no conflicting tag) before the user answers.
The armour decision is written into the archery spec as a numbered rule.
The raw stamina number (12) is parked in the parking lot for L3, not written as a spec rule.

The reply has four parts in order: a one-line state (system, layer, status), the rules recorded by ID with their text, reversals and conflicts, and what is needed from the user as questions sized to one decision.
